basis: 17 of 25 tracked indices rose in their latest session.

headline.layman: The Fed left rates alone, but traders think a hike in December is likely. US stocks edged up even though Google's parent Alphabet dropped 10% after a weak report.

global.title: Fed holds, hike odds build, Big Tech splits

status.technical: The Fed held rates at 3.75%–4% in a 10–2 vote, citing persistent inflation (Mint). S&P 500 closed up 0.28%, Dow 0.19%, Nasdaq 0.27%. Brent fell 2.86% to 110.62; the US 10-year yield closed at 5.05.
status.layman: The Fed kept its main rate unchanged after a vote. US stocks ended slightly higher. Oil prices eased on the day but remain very high.

consequence.technical: Bloomberg reported Chairman Warsh left the Fed on track to raise rates again this year without explicit guidance; Moneycontrol reported a 90% chance of a December hike. If a hike comes, borrowing costs would rise further.
consequence.layman: Traders think the Fed may raise rates again in December. If it does, loans and credit could get more expensive. Nothing is certain.

impact.technical: Yahoo Finance said the decision matters for bank accounts, loans, credit cards and investments. Mint cited crude oil near $115 a barrel and rising US bond yields as risks for Indian equities. Evidence on other sectors is thin.
impact.layman: Savers, borrowers and investors all feel Fed decisions. Higher oil prices and bond yields add pressure for some markets, such as India. Evidence beyond that is thin.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after ordinary days the S&P 500 rose the next day 54% of 845 times and over the next 5 days 59% of 843 times. Look-alike days rose over the next 21 days 4 of 5 times.
outlook.layman: Looking at history, after quiet days like this the S&P 500 rose the next day a bit more than half the time. That is a pattern from the past, not a forecast.

regions.title: Americas: US edges up, Brazil sells off

status.technical: US indices closed higher (S&P 500 0.28%, Nasdaq 0.27%). WSJ reported the Nasdaq edged lower intraday as tech euphoria from Anthropic's IPO filing fizzled. Bovespa fell 2.68% in one day and 17.19% over five days.
status.layman: US stocks ended a little higher. Brazil's main stock index fell sharply over the week. Bloomberg separately reported that the incumbent Lula won Sunday's presidential election.

consequence.technical: Bloomberg said Trump sheltering Flavio Bolsonaro risks tensions with Brazil. If US–Brazil relations sour, Brazilian assets could stay under pressure; the notes do not tie the Bovespa fall to this.
consequence.layman: If US–Brazil relations sour, Brazil's market could stay jittery. The news does not say that caused the drop.

impact.technical: Bloomberg reported Petrobras lifted production to a record in the third quarter, helping Brazil weather energy disruptions from the Iran war. Evidence on what drove the Bovespa fall is thin.
impact.layman: Brazil's oil producer Petrobras hit record output, per Bloomberg. The news does not explain why the wider market fell.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after one-day falls larger than 1 standard deviation, the Bovespa rose the next day 47% of 158 times and over the next 5 days 50% of 157 times.
outlook.layman: History shows big drops are followed by gains about half the time. That is a pattern, not a forecast.

regions.title: Asia-Pacific: China weak, Korea chips surge

status.technical: Shanghai Composite fell 1.33% and Shenzhen Component 2.50% on 2026-10-27. FT reported the CSI 300 entered a technical bear market and state funds bought stocks. KOSPI rose 3.09% after SK Hynix's record third-quarter profit lifted chip shares (Mint).
status.layman: Chinese stocks fell, and the Financial Times said state-linked funds stepped in to buy. Korea's market rose as chipmakers cheered a record profit from SK Hynix.

consequence.technical: SCMP quoted analysts saying state buying will be insufficient to engineer a durable rally in China's market. If so, weakness there could persist; this is the analysts' view, not a forecast.
consequence.layman: Analysts quoted by SCMP say government buying alone is unlikely to produce a lasting rebound in China.

impact.technical: The HKMA held its base rate at 4.25% after the Fed decision (SCMP). Bloomberg reported Japan's credit risk jumped the most since 2022, pressuring its bond market. Nikkei closed up 1.73% on 2026-10-27.
impact.layman: Hong Kong kept its key rate unchanged. Bloomberg reported Japan's credit risk jumped the most since 2022, pressuring its bonds.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after one-day falls larger than 1 standard deviation, the Shanghai Composite rose the next day 50% of 152 times and over the next 5 days 51% of 151 times.
outlook.layman: History shows big drops in Shanghai are followed by gains about half the time. That is a pattern, not a forecast.

status.technical: The Fed held at 3.75%–4% in a 10–2 vote (Mint); the Guardian said inflation remains above 3%. Bloomberg said Warsh left the Fed on track to hike again this year. Moneycontrol reported a 90% chance of a December hike.
status.layman: The Fed kept rates steady but inflation is still high. Reports say another increase could come in December.

consequence.technical: CNBC reported Treasury Secretary Bessent said it is 'not necessarily' a mistake if the Fed hikes again. If the Fed does hike in December, borrowing costs would rise further.
consequence.layman: A US Treasury official said another hike would not necessarily be a mistake. If it happens, borrowing gets pricier.

impact.technical: Fed decisions touch bank accounts, loans, credit cards and investments (Yahoo Finance). Mint said the Fed outcome was already priced in for Indian equities.
impact.layman: Fed decisions affect savings, loans and cards. Mint said Indian investors had already expected this outcome.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after one-day rises larger than 1 standard deviation, the US 10-year yield rose the next day 51% of 184 times. It closed at 5.05.
outlook.layman: History shows yields rise after big jumps about half the time. That is a pattern, not a forecast.

drivers.title: Oil near $110 and the Iran war

status.technical: Brent closed at 110.62, down 2.86% on the day but up 24.25% over three months; WTI closed at 101.94. Bloomberg tied energy disruption to the Iran war; WSJ reported Vance engaged Iran to revive peace talks.
status.layman: Oil is very expensive. Bloomberg linked that to the Iran war, and WSJ reported efforts to restart peace talks.

consequence.technical: Mint cited crude oil near $115 a barrel as a bigger risk to Indian equities than the Fed. Reuters said oil prices weighed on European shares. If oil stays high, these pressures may persist.
consequence.layman: If oil stays high, markets that import energy, like India, may stay under pressure.

impact.technical: Mint said the Canadian heavy-oil discount exceeded $30, the widest relative to US futures in more than four years. Mint also named rupee weakness as a risk for India. Evidence on other sectors is thin.
impact.layman: High oil hurts importers and can weaken their currencies. Canada's heavy oil is selling at a big discount to US prices.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after one-day falls larger than 1 standard deviation, Brent rose the next day 49% of 168 times and over the next 5 days 54% of 168 times.
outlook.layman: History shows oil rises after big drops about half the time. That is a pattern, not a forecast.

drivers.title: Big Tech earnings split on AI spending

status.technical: CNBC reported Alphabet sank 10% after its first top-and-bottom-line miss in nearly four years; it held 2026 capex unchanged and expects a significant increase in 2027. CNBC reported Microsoft rose 4% on Azure revenue growth of 48%.
status.layman: Google's parent Alphabet fell 10% after a weak report, while Microsoft rose 4% on strong cloud growth.

consequence.technical: The Financial Times said Alphabet's $51bn AI outlay deepened cash burn. If AI spending keeps rising while sales undershoot, cash-burn concerns may persist; if cloud growth holds, as at Microsoft, investors may keep rewarding it.
consequence.layman: If a company spends heavily on AI but sales disappoint, investors may punish it. Strong cloud growth, like Microsoft's, was rewarded.

impact.technical: CNBC reported Nvidia faces a DOJ inquiry over its $12.9 billion Hugging Face purchase, and said the Magnificent Seven's correlation is breaking down. Evidence on wider market effects is thin.
impact.layman: Big Tech stocks no longer move together, per CNBC. Nvidia faces a US Justice Department inquiry into a big deal.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after ordinary days the Nasdaq rose the next day 55% of 825 times and over the next 5 days 59% of 823 times. Look-alike days rose over 5 days only 1 of 5 times.
outlook.layman: History shows the Nasdaq rises after quiet days a bit more than half the time. That is a pattern, not a forecast.

status.technical: Mint reported SK Hynix's record third-quarter profit lifted Asian and US chip shares, with AMD and Micron gaining up to 5%. Economic Times said a chipmaker resurgence helped US stocks end higher.
status.layman: A record profit at SK Hynix lifted chip stocks in Asia and the US, per Mint.

consequence.technical: If chip earnings keep beating expectations, AI optimism could keep supporting chip shares; the Financial Times noted chip earnings power averaged higher. This is conditional, not a forecast.
consequence.layman: If chipmakers keep reporting strong profits, chip stocks may keep getting support. Nothing is guaranteed.

impact.technical: KOSPI heavyweights Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix both rose on the day (hw data). Evidence on wider effects is thin.
impact.layman: Korea's two biggest listed names both rose on the day. The notes say little about wider effects.

outlook.layman: History shows the KOSPI rises after quiet days a bit more than half the time. That is a pattern, not a forecast.
